name: Cargo
tagline: Design-focused website publishing with flexible layouts and type tools

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Site Builder
tiers.limits: One account can design and publish one or many public sites; real-time multi-user editing; 1 custom-domain connection
tiers.notes: Annual price is $168/year. Students, teachers and related administrators can qualify for free use through Cargo's education program.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no general free published-site tier; sites are free to build privately for any duration; verified students/teachers can receive free use
pricing.billingTerms: monthly or annual ($19/month monthly; $14/month billed yearly)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Only 1 custom-domain connection is included; each additional domain costs $3/month on monthly billing or $2/month on yearly billing. Commerce payment processing still incurs the connected processor's fees.

verdictSummary: The visible creative website builder loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Cargo earns its keep through editor, CMS, hosting, polish, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a focused creative website builder generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Cargo: A single site is easy to code. People pay for safe ongoing edits, templates, publishing, domains, collaboration, and no-maintenance hosting.
ongoingBurden: Maintain responsive rendering, browser compatibility, deployment, domains, forms, spam protection, backups, and editor migrations.

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: Freeform hosted design, responsive layouts and custom domains free; Cargo's typography cult is not included.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optional npm-installed Plasmic CLI for React code generation and deployment in your own repository
facts.engines: Plasmic AI (beta); the official site does not name its underlying model provider
facts.dataFormat: Hosted projects and CMS records in Plasmic Cloud; codegen writes React components plus plasmic.json and plasmic.lock into the user's repository
facts.gapVsPaid: Plasmic does not match Cargo's tightly curated typography, templates and creative-community taste.
facts.setupBlocker: Free hosted output keeps Plasmic branding; codegen/self-deployment requires a Node/React project and deployment workflow

alternatives.name: Silex
alternatives.desc: Freeform visual publishing with static export; less art-school mystique, considerably more ownership.

facts.install: Use the hosted editor with a GitLab login, install the desktop alpha, or run the official Docker setup
facts.engines: Optional desktop MCP workflow can connect to Ollama, OpenCode, Goose or Claude Code
facts.dataFormat: Project JSON and assets in GitLab, FTP or local storage; publishing produces ordinary static HTML, CSS and JavaScript
facts.gapVsPaid: Silex gives less typographic curation, animation polish and creative-community context than Cargo.
facts.setupBlocker: The stable hosted route starts with a GitLab account; the desktop build is still labelled alpha

alternatives.name: Webstudio
alternatives.desc: A visual canvas with honest CSS and CMS connections; the free custom-domain route means self-hosting.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; alternatively export the project or deploy the self-hosted builder/site
facts.engines: Webstudio Inception AI and MCP integrations; the hosted model provider is not named in official documentation
facts.dataFormat: Projects and assets live in Webstudio Cloud when hosted there; export/self-host routes produce source or static assets under the user's deployment
facts.gapVsPaid: Webstudio lacks Cargo's distinctive typography, templates and curated creative community.
facts.setupBlocker: The free cloud plan publishes only to a Webstudio subdomain; a free custom domain requires export or self-hosting

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A page-builder framework, not a finished publishing service, despite the very convincing playground.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Cargo is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Cargo, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a focused creative website builder generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: general-purpose visual editing; large template and component libraries; CMS collaboration and client handoff.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
